# Webhooks

Source: <https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/webhooks>

Each time an order, an application or an allocation changes state, or more of an order fills, we create an event. We send the event to your webhook endpoint as an HTTPS `POST`, and you can also read it from `GET /v1/events` for 30 days.

The format follows [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com), so any Standard Webhooks library can verify our signatures.

## Register your endpoint

We register your endpoint for you. There's no API for it. [Send us](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/support) the URL, and we send its signing secret to your technical contact through a [one-time link](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/support#how-keys-and-secrets-reach-you). You have one endpoint in each environment: the sandbox and live each have their own endpoint and their own secret. The URL must meet these rules:

| Rule | Example |
|---|---|
| It uses `https`. | `https://hooks.example.com/matamba` |
| It has no username or password in it. | Not `https://user:pass@hooks.example.com/` |
| It has no query string. | Not `https://hooks.example.com/matamba?token=abc` |
| Its host is a public address. | Not a private, loopback, link-local or other reserved address |

We check the address each time we connect, after the host name resolves. We don't use a proxy, and we don't follow redirects.

We send events from our server's own IP address, which we give you with the signing secret. You can allowlist it on your firewall, but you don't have to: the signature proves an event came from us. If we move servers, the address changes, and we email your technical contact at least seven days before it does. An allowlist adds to checking the signature and never replaces it.

You receive the events created after we register your endpoint. Events from before then are in `GET /v1/events`. If you move to a new URL, we keep your secret, and events that are still due go to the new URL.

## What we send

Each event is a `POST` with a JSON body and these headers:

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |
| `User-Agent` | `Matamba-Webhooks/1.0` |
| `webhook-id` | The event's ID, such as `msg_5f0c2a9e7b1d4c3a8e6f0b12`. It's the same on every retry, so use it to ignore an event you've already processed. |
| `webhook-timestamp` | When we sent this attempt, in Unix seconds. |
| `webhook-signature` | One or more signatures, separated by spaces, each written as `v1,` and a base64 value. |

The body is the event: the same object `GET /v1/events` lists, with `object` and `id` included. Its `id` is the `webhook-id` header. Here it is formatted for reading:

```json Event body
{
  "object": "event",
  "id": "msg_5f0c2a9e7b1d4c3a8e6f0b12",
  "type": "order.filled",
  "timestamp": "2026-09-25T06:13:02Z",
  "version": 2,
  "data": {
    "object": "order",
    "id": "ord_62jxryztxctob7uopekg",
    "state": "filled",
    "account": "1000000001",
    "symbol": "DANGCEM",
    "side": "buy",
    "quantity": 10,
    "type": "market",
    "time_in_force": "day",
    "price_kobo": null,
    "filled_quantity": 10,
    "exchange_order_id": "1790316754123",
    "reason": null,
    "reject_reason": null,
    "created_at": "2026-09-25T06:12:34Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-09-25T06:13:02Z",
    "filled_at": "2026-09-25T06:13:02Z",
    "average_fill_price_kobo_decimal": "47500",
    "client_reference": null
  }
}
```

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `object` | Always `event`. |
| `id` | The event's ID, the same as the `webhook-id` header. |
| `type` | What changed and its new state. See the table below. |
| `timestamp` | The `updated_at` of the order, application or allocation. |
| `version` | A number that increases with each of your events and is never reused. It is yours alone: your orders, applications and allocations share it, and other partners' events never move it. Events can arrive out of order, so compare `version` per object: for each order, application or allocation, ignore an event whose `version` is lower than the last one you applied to that same object. |
| `data` | The order, application or allocation as the change left it, exactly as its `GET` returned it at that moment. |

### Event types

| Type | Sent when |
|---|---|
| `order.cancelled`, `order.expired`, `order.filled`, `order.partially_filled`, `order.pending`, `order.refused`, `order.rejected`, `order.uncertain` | An order moves to that state. An order that fills in parts sends `order.partially_filled` each time we find more of it filled. Parts that fill between two of our checks arrive as one event, and an order that completes within one check sends only `order.filled`. Read `filled_quantity`, not the count of events. |
| `application.documents_required`, `application.opened`, `application.refused`, `application.rejected`, `application.submitted`, `application.uncertain`, `application.unplaced` | An application moves to that state. `application.opened` carries the new `account`. |
| `allocation.booked`, `allocation.refused`, `allocation.rejected`, `allocation.uncertain` | An allocation moves to that state. `allocation.booked` means the money is in the account's balance at the broker. |

Every state after `sending` sends an event, including the outcome the create request already returned to you. There's no event for `sending` itself, and none for a credit or a withdrawal entry in your wallet: read them in `GET /v1/wallet/transfers`.

New event types can appear without notice. Ignore any type you don't handle. See [Versioning](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/versioning).

## Verify each event

Check the signature before you trust an event. Anyone who learns your URL can send it a request.

**Read the raw body**

Use the body bytes exactly as they arrived. Parsing the JSON and writing it out again changes the bytes, and the signature won't match.

**Check the timestamp**

Reject the event if `webhook-timestamp` is more than 5 minutes before or after your server's clock. This is the default tolerance in the Standard Webhooks libraries, and it stops an old event from being replayed. We stamp each attempt when we send it, so a retry carries a fresh timestamp.

**Build the signed content**

Join the `webhook-id` header, the `webhook-timestamp` header and the raw body with a full stop between each: `id.timestamp.body`.

**Compute the signature**

Your secret starts with `whsec_`. Base64 decode the part after `whsec_`, and use the decoded bytes as the key. Don't use the secret text itself. Compute an HMAC-SHA256 of the signed content with that key, and base64 encode the result.

**Compare**

Split `webhook-signature` on spaces. Accept the event if any entry is `v1,` followed by your value. Compare with a constant-time function, not `==`.

```javascript Node.js
import crypto from "node:crypto";

const TOLERANCE_SECONDS = 5 * 60;

// headers: the request's headers, with lowercase names.
// rawBody: a Buffer holding the body exactly as it arrived.
export function verifyWebhook(secret, headers, rawBody) {
  const id = headers["webhook-id"];
  const timestamp = headers["webhook-timestamp"];
  const signatures = headers["webhook-signature"];
  if (!id || !timestamp || !signatures || !secret.startsWith("whsec_")) {
    return false;
  }

  const sent = Number(timestamp);
  const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  if (!Number.isInteger(sent) || Math.abs(now - sent) > TOLERANCE_SECONDS) {
    return false;
  }

  const key = Buffer.from(secret.slice("whsec_".length), "base64");
  const expected = crypto
    .createHmac("sha256", key)
    .update(`${id}.${timestamp}.`)
    .update(rawBody)
    .digest();

  return signatures.split(" ").some((entry) => {
    const [version, value] = entry.split(",");
    if (version !== "v1" || !value) {
      return false;
    }
    const given = Buffer.from(value, "base64");
    return given.length === expected.length && crypto.timingSafeEqual(given, expected);
  });
}
```

```python Python
import base64
import hashlib
import hmac
import time

TOLERANCE_SECONDS = 5 * 60

def verify_webhook(secret: str, headers, raw_body: bytes) -> bool:
    """headers: the request's headers. raw_body: the body exactly as it arrived."""
    msg_id = headers.get("webhook-id")
    timestamp = headers.get("webhook-timestamp")
    signatures = headers.get("webhook-signature")
    if not msg_id or not timestamp or not signatures or not secret.startswith("whsec_"):
        return False

    try:
        sent = int(timestamp)
    except ValueError:
        return False
    if abs(time.time() - sent) > TOLERANCE_SECONDS:
        return False

    key = base64.b64decode(secret[len("whsec_"):])
    signed = f"{msg_id}.{timestamp}.".encode() + raw_body
    expected = base64.b64encode(hmac.new(key, signed, hashlib.sha256).digest())

    for entry in signatures.split(" "):
        version, _, value = entry.partition(",")
        # Bytes, not str: compare_digest raises on a str that isn't ASCII.
        if version == "v1" and hmac.compare_digest(value.encode(), expected):
            return True
    return False
```

```go Go
package webhooks

import (
	"crypto/hmac"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/base64"
	"net/http"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

const tolerance = 5 * time.Minute

// Verify reports whether an event came from us. body is the request body
// exactly as it arrived.
func Verify(secret string, h http.Header, body []byte) bool {
	id, ts, signatures := h.Get("webhook-id"), h.Get("webhook-timestamp"), h.Get("webhook-signature")
	encoded, isSecret := strings.CutPrefix(secret, "whsec_")
	if id == "" || signatures == "" || !isSecret {
		return false
	}

	sent, err := strconv.ParseInt(ts, 10, 64)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	if age := time.Since(time.Unix(sent, 0)); age > tolerance || age < -tolerance {
		return false
	}

	key, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(encoded)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, key)
	mac.Write([]byte(id + "." + ts + "."))
	mac.Write(body)
	expected := mac.Sum(nil)

	for _, entry := range strings.Split(signatures, " ") {
		version, value, _ := strings.Cut(entry, ",")
		given, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(value)
		if version == "v1" && err == nil && hmac.Equal(given, expected) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}
```

## Respond

Return any `2xx` status within 10 seconds. We read up to 64 KiB of your response and ignore what it says. Save the event and do the work after you respond, so a slow task doesn't turn into a failed delivery:

```javascript Node.js
// Express, with the body kept as it arrived: app.use(express.raw({ type: "application/json" }))
app.post("/webhooks/matamba", async (req, res) => {
  if (!verifyWebhook(process.env.MATAMBA_WEBHOOK_SECRET, req.headers, req.body)) {
    return res.sendStatus(400);
  }
  const event = JSON.parse(req.body);
  await saveEvent(event); // your store, keyed by event.id: a retry repeats it
  res.sendStatus(200); // answer first
  processLater(event.id); // then do the work, off the request
});
```

## Retries

We send each new event within about 5 seconds of recording the change. We try each event on this schedule until one attempt succeeds:

| Attempt | About this long after the change |
|---|---|
| 1 | At once |
| 2 | 1 minute |
| 3 | 6 minutes |
| 4 | 21 minutes |
| 5 | 51 minutes |
| 6 | 1 hour and 51 minutes |
| 7 | 3 hours and 51 minutes |
| 8 | 7 hours and 51 minutes |
| 9 | 15 hours and 51 minutes |
| 10 | 27 hours and 51 minutes |

The tenth attempt, 27 hours and 51 minutes after the change, is the last. The hour after it allows for delays between attempts. Until then an event can still be delivered, such as by a paused endpoint's probe. We stop sending an event 28 hours and 51 minutes after the change it describes. It stays in `GET /v1/events`. If your endpoint was down for longer, you can also [ask us](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/support) to send the events we stopped sending since a time you name. We send the same events again, with the same `webhook-id`, and a new 28 hours and 51 minutes of retries from when we start.

| Your endpoint | What we do |
|---|---|
| Returns `2xx` | Delivered. |
| Doesn't answer within 10 seconds, can't be reached, or returns a redirect, `408`, `429` or `5xx` | A failed attempt. After 3 of these in a row, we pause your endpoint and try one event about once a minute. When one succeeds, we send what's waiting, oldest first. |
| Returns any other `4xx` | This event failed, and we retry it on the schedule above. We keep sending your other events. |

While your endpoint is paused, each event's own retry schedule doesn't apply: each probe is the oldest event waiting. A pause doesn't change when we stop sending an event.

Delivery is at least once. You can receive the same event twice, and a retried event can arrive after a newer one. Use `webhook-id` to ignore duplicates, and compare `version` per object to ignore stale changes.

## Catch up on missed events

`GET /v1/events` lists every event for 30 days, oldest first, whether or not your endpoint accepted it. Use it after downtime, or instead of a webhook endpoint.

1. Call `GET /v1/events` without a cursor. Pass `limit` to set the page size, from 1 to 100. The default is 25.
2. Process the events, then store the `next_cursor` from the response. If your first call returns no events, `next_cursor` is null, so call again without a cursor next time.
3. Next time, pass that value as `cursor`. When there are no new events, you get an empty page and the same cursor back, so keep it for next time.

A cursor is a place in the list, not an event, so it never expires. From a cursor older than the 30 days, the list starts at the oldest event we still hold.

If you poll instead of receiving webhooks, call `GET /v1/events` every 30 seconds.

## Rotate your secret

We rotate your secret when you ask. For 24 hours after a rotation, we sign every event with both the new and the old secret, so `webhook-signature` carries two entries, the new one first. Switch your server to the new secret within those 24 hours. We can start another rotation only after the 24 hours end, unless your secret has leaked: then we rotate it with no overlap, and the old secret stops signing at once. See [If a signing secret leaks](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/support#if-a-signing-secret-leaks).

## Test webhooks in the sandbox

The sandbox sends events the same way live does, under the same rules:

- Your endpoint needs a public `https` URL that meets [the rules](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/webhooks#register-your-endpoint). To receive events on your own machine, use a tunnelling service, which gives your local server a public HTTPS address and forwards requests to it.
- Your sandbox endpoint has its own secret. Keep it apart from your live one.

To rehearse the failures your endpoint will meet in live:

| To rehearse | Do this |
|---|---|
| A retry | Answer an event with a `5xx`. We try it again on the [retry schedule](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/webhooks#retries), with the same `webhook-id` and a fresh timestamp. |
| A paused endpoint | Keep answering with a `5xx`, or stop your server. We pause your endpoint as described under [Retries](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/webhooks#retries). Answer `2xx` again, and what was waiting arrives, oldest first. |
| One refused event | Answer one event with a `400`. We retry that event alone, and keep sending the others. |
| Catching up | Stop your server, place an order, then read `GET /v1/events` from your stored cursor. |
